models.name: discussion_board_users
models.description:
Registered user accounts with email/password credentials and profile information.

This table stores the core identity information for regular users of the discussion board platform. Each record represents an individual user account with authentication credentials and profile data. Users can create articles, write comments, and participate in discussions across various sections.

The table serves as the root identity record for the user actor type and is referenced by session management, password reset workflows, and content creation entities. User profiles display the user's display name, biography, and activity history including articles and comments they have authored.

{@link discussion_board_user_sessions} tracks user login sessions.
{@link discussion_board_user_password_resets} handles password recovery.
{@link discussion_board_user_email_verifications} manages email confirmation.
{@link discussion_board_articles} stores articles authored by users.
{@link discussion_board_comments} stores comments written by users.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all user accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for user authentication. Stored using industry-standard hashing algorithms.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on user profiles and alongside user-generated content.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biography text describing the user's background, interests, or expertise.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted, allowing for account recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_user_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for user authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table stores active user sessions with JWT tokens for secure authentication. Each session tracks connection context including IP address, user agent, and referrer information for security auditing. Sessions maintain both access tokens for API calls and refresh tokens for token renewal.

The session lifecycle is managed through creation and expiration timestamps, allowing for secure session invalidation and automatic cleanup of expired sessions. This table supports the authentication system's requirement to maintain secure session state while users are logged in.

Sessions are child entities of {@link discussion_board_users} and support the platform's authentication security requirements.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for API authentication.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for token renewal.

plainFields.name: ip

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser or client user agent string.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header for connection context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at

plainFields.name: last_accessed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last session activity.

models.name: discussion_board_user_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for user account recovery with expiration tracking.

This table stores temporary tokens that allow users to reset their passwords when they forget their credentials. Each token is associated with a specific user account and has a limited validity period for security purposes.

The system generates a unique token when a user requests a password reset and sends it via email. When the user clicks the reset link, the system validates the token against this table before allowing password changes.

Security considerations include automatic token expiration and one-time usage to prevent unauthorized access. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user account requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique reset token generated for password recovery. This token is sent to the user's email and must be used within the expiration period.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token expires and becomes invalid. After this time, the token cannot be used for password recovery.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was successfully used to change the password. Null indicates the token is still available for use.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset record was soft deleted for security purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_user_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for user registration confirmation.

This table stores verification tokens that are sent to users during the registration process to confirm their email addresses. Each token is unique and has a limited validity period to ensure security. Once a user successfully verifies their email using the token, the verification record is marked as completed and the user account becomes fully activated.

Tokens are generated when users register and are sent via email. Users must click the verification link containing the token within the expiration period to complete their registration. This process prevents fake registrations and ensures email address validity.

{@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user account requiring email verification. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to the user's email address for confirmation.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user successfully verified their email address using this token.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions

Each session records connection context such as IP address, user agent, and referrer information for security auditing. Sessions have expiration tracking to enforce security policies and prevent indefinite access.

The relationship with {@link discussion_board_admins} establishes the administrator ownership of sessions, allowing multiple concurrent sessions per administrator while maintaining individual session management. This supports features like session revocation, multi-device access, and security monitoring for administrator accounts.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_password_resets

models.name: discussion_board_super_admins
models.description:
Super administrator accounts with elevated privileges and system-wide control.

Represents the highest privilege level in the system with capabilities to promote/demote other administrators, manage system-wide settings, and perform all administrative functions. Super administrators have complete control over the platform and can manage regular administrators.

This table stores authentication credentials and privilege information for super administrators. Each super administrator has a unique email address and password hash for secure login. The table maintains audit trails through standard temporal fields.

Super administrators can perform all actions available to regular administrators plus additional system-wide management capabilities. They are responsible for maintaining the administrator hierarchy and ensuring platform security.

{@link discussion_board_super_admin_sessions.id} tracks login sessions, {@link discussion_board_super_admin_password_resets.id} handles password recovery, and {@link discussion_board_super_admin_email_verifications.id} manages email verification workflows.

Each session belongs to exactly one super administrator and contains the necessary authentication tokens along with audit information for security monitoring.

The session records enable secure authentication flow management, token expiration tracking, and connection auditing for compliance purposes. Sessions are managed through the authentication system rather than direct user CRUD operations.

models.name: discussion_board_super_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for super administrator account recovery with expiration tracking.

This table stores temporary tokens that allow super administrators to reset their passwords securely. Each token is associated with a specific super administrator account and has a limited validity period to prevent unauthorized access. The system generates these tokens when a super administrator requests a password reset and invalidates them after use or expiration.

Tokens are single-use only and automatically expire after a configured time period. The table tracks when tokens are used to prevent replay attacks and ensures that each reset request can only be completed once. This security mechanism protects super administrator accounts while maintaining accessibility for legitimate password recovery scenarios.

{@link discussion_board_super_admins.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_admin_id

plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_super_admin_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for super administrator registration confirmation.

Stores secure verification tokens used during super administrator registration process to validate email ownership. Each token is tied to a specific super administrator account and includes expiration tracking for security. Verification status is tracked to prevent multiple verification attempts.

Relationships:
- Belongs to one {@link discussion_board_super_admins.super admin account}
- Verification token is used once and then expired

Security Considerations:
- Tokens are hashed before storage
- Expiration prevents indefinite verification windows
- One token per pending verification to prevent token reuse

plainFields.name: token_hash

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this validation token expires and can no longer be used for verification. Typically set to 24 hours after creation for security.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was successfully completed using this token. Null indicates pending verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was created as part of registration process.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was last updated, typically when verification is completed.

This table stores all configurable parameters that control the behavior and features of the discussion board platform. Administrators can modify these settings to customize platform functionality, enable/disable features, and adjust operational parameters without requiring code changes.

Each configuration entry represents a specific system parameter that influences platform behavior, such as rate limits, content policies, display settings, or feature toggles. The configuration system provides a centralized way to manage platform settings across all system components.

Configurations are organized by functional areas and can be modified by authorized administrators through the system administration interface.

models.name: discussion_board_audit_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail for all administrative actions and system events across the discussion board platform.

This table captures detailed information about every significant action performed by users, administrators, and the system itself. Each record includes the actor who performed the action, the type of action, the target entity affected, timestamp information, and additional metadata specific to the action type.

The audit trail serves multiple purposes including compliance monitoring, security investigation, system debugging, and user accountability. All records are append-only and cannot be modified once created to ensure the integrity of the audit trail.

Key relationships:
- References actor tables ({@link discussion_board_users}, {@link discussion_board_admins}, {@link discussion_board_super_admins}) for actor identification
- Captures actions across all system components including articles, comments, sections, and user management
- Supports detailed investigation through comprehensive metadata storage

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_promotion_approvals
models.description:
Stores approval records for administrator promotion requests with reviewer information and decision details.

Each record represents a single approval or rejection decision made by an administrator on a promotion request. This table maintains a complete audit trail of all promotion decisions, including who made the decision, when it was made, and the rationale behind it.

The table supports the administrator promotion workflow by tracking the entire lifecycle of promotion requests from submission to final decision. It ensures accountability and transparency in the promotion process by recording all decision-making activities.

This table works in conjunction with {@link discussion_board_administrator_promotion_requests} which stores the original promotion requests, and references {@link discussion_board_admins} for the reviewing administrator information. It also maintains a relationship to the parent {@link discussion_board_administrators} table to track which administrator record is affected by the promotion decision.

models.name: discussion_board_content_moderation_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail of content moderation actions performed by administrators.

This table logs all moderation activities including article deletions, comment deletions, and other content management actions. Each record captures the moderator, action type, target content, timestamp, and reason for the moderation action.

models.name: discussion_board_error_logs

This table captures all system errors that occur within the discussion board platform, providing detailed information for debugging, monitoring, and performance analysis. Each error record includes the error type, stack trace, request context, and severity level to help developers identify and resolve issues quickly.

The error logs support the system's performance monitoring requirements by tracking error frequency and patterns, and they provide security auditing capabilities by recording unexpected system behavior. Errors are categorized by severity to prioritize debugging efforts and maintain system stability.

This table integrates with the broader Systematic component infrastructure, providing essential debugging information that complements the performance metrics and audit logs maintained in other Systematic tables.

models.name: discussion_board_article_images
models.description:
Central repository for article image attachments with comprehensive lifecycle management. Each image record maintains metadata for efficient retrieval and display while supporting versioning, status tracking, and independent management operations.

This table enables system-wide image operations including search across articles, bulk management, and status tracking. Images can be independently managed while maintaining referential integrity with parent articles. The design supports complete image lifecycle from upload through archival or deletion.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article that this image is attached to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: attachment_file_id
plainFields.description: Reference to the centralized file storage containing the actual image binary data and metadata. {@link discussion_board_attachment_files.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the image in the workflow: 'uploaded', 'processing', 'active', 'archived', 'deleted'.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Order in which images should be displayed within the article content.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Alternative text for accessibility and SEO purposes describing the image content.

plainFields.name: caption
plainFields.description: Optional caption text displayed below the image for additional context.

models.name: discussion_board_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table implementing the tagging system for articles. This table enables multiple free-text tags to be associated with each article through a many-to-many relationship. Tags are stored as free text and support flexible categorization of article content.

The tagging system allows users to add descriptive labels to their articles, making content more discoverable through tag-based filtering and search. Each tag association is unique per article, preventing duplicate tags on the same article while allowing the same tag to be used across multiple articles.

This table serves as the bridge between {@link discussion_board_articles} and the tag values, maintaining referential integrity while enabling efficient tag-based queries and filtering operations.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the associated article. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: tag_name
plainFields.description: Free-text tag name assigned to the article. Users can create custom tags to categorize content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was associated with the article.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag association was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag association was soft-deleted, allowing for tag removal tracking.

models.name: discussion_board_article_view_stats
models.description:
Tracks view statistics and engagement metrics for articles. This table records view counts, unique viewers, and temporal patterns for article analytics. Provides data for article popularity, user engagement tracking, and content performance analysis.

Each record represents view statistics aggregates for a specific article, including total view count, unique viewer count, and calculation fields for derived metrics. The data supports analytics dashboards, content recommendations, and article performance insights.

This table integrates with {@link discussion_board_articles} to provide comprehensive article analytics and requires {@link discussion_board_article_view_stat_events} for granular view tracking and 3NF compliance.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article being tracked. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: total_view_count
plainFields.description: Total number of views for the article, including repeat views from the same user.

plainFields.name: unique_viewer_count
plainFields.description: Number of distinct users who have viewed the article.

plainFields.name: last_viewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent view of the article.

plainFields.name: average_time_spent_seconds
plainFields.description: Average time users spend viewing the article in seconds, calculated from view events.

plainFields.name: total_time_spent_seconds
plainFields.description: Total accumulated time spent by all viewers on the article.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view statistics record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view statistics record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_article_favorites
models.description:
Junction table representing user bookmarking of articles. Each record indicates that a specific user has favorited a specific article, creating a many-to-many relationship between users and articles.

This table enables users to save articles of interest for quick access later. It also supports analytics on article popularity based on favorite counts. The relationship is unique per user-article pair to prevent duplicate favorites.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_users.id} for the user who favorited the article, {@link discussion_board_articles.id} for the article being favorited.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user who favorited the article. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article that was favorited. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user favorited the article.

models.name: discussion_board_article_drafts
models.description:
Stores draft versions of articles before publication with auto-recovery features.

This table manages article drafts that users create before publishing their content to the main discussion board. Drafts are independent entities that users can create, edit, and delete separately from published articles. When a draft is published, it becomes associated with a main article record.

Key features include:
- Draft-specific metadata for auto-recovery functionality
- Independent lifecycle management from published articles
- Support for draft-specific workflows and status tracking
- Association with published articles when finalized

Drafts are managed through the article creation workflow and provide users with the ability to save work in progress without committing to publication. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the published article when this draft becomes finalized. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: draft_title
plainFields.description: Working title of the draft, which may differ from the final published article title.

plainFields.name: draft_content
plainFields.description: Working content of the draft, which may differ from the final published article content.

plainFields.name: draft_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the draft. Values: 'draft', 'published', 'archived'.

plainFields.name: last_saved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last auto-save operation for recovery purposes.

plainFields.name: recovery_data
plainFields.description: JSON data for auto-recovery functionality, storing incremental changes and edit history.

plainFields.name: draft_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the draft was first created.

plainFields.name: draft_updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the draft was last modified.

plainFields.name: draft_deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the draft was soft-deleted, allowing for recovery.

models.name: discussion_board_article_image_files
models.description:
Stores comprehensive file metadata for images attached to articles, providing detailed file information and lifecycle management for image attachments. This table serves as a subsidiary entity to {@link discussion_board_article_images}, containing technical file details separate from the image content itself.

The table captures essential file metadata including filename, size, MIME type, and storage information, enabling proper file management and retrieval. It supports the image attachment system by providing the technical foundation for file operations while maintaining referential integrity with the parent image entity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_image_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article image entity. {@link discussion_board_article_images.id}

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded image file as provided by the user.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the image file in bytes, used for storage management and download size estimation.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image file (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif).

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Server-side storage path where the image file is physically stored.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename provided during upload, preserved for user reference.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file metadata was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file metadata was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_article_view_stat_events
models.description:
Records individual article view events for granular analytics and engagement tracking. Each event captures detailed information about when an article was viewed, by which user session, and for how long. This table supports the aggregated view statistics in {@link discussion_board_article_view_stats} while maintaining 3NF compliance through proper event-level tracking.

The table enables detailed analytics such as user engagement patterns, popular content analysis, and reader behavior tracking. View events are append-only records that provide the foundation for comprehensive article performance metrics and user activity analysis.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the viewed article. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user session that viewed the article. {@link discussion_board_user_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view event was recorded.

plainFields.name: view_duration_seconds
plainFields.description: Duration of the view event in seconds, measuring how long the user engaged with the article content.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Core comment entity storing user comments on articles. Contains comment content, author information, article association, and management metadata. Users can create, edit, and delete their comments independently.

Comments are single-level only (no nested replies) as specified in requirements. Each comment belongs to exactly one article and one author. The system tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit purposes.

This table serves as the foundation for comment functionality including display, editing, deletion, and moderation. {@link discussion_board_users.id} for author association and {@link discussion_board_articles.id} for article linkage.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Author of the comment. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article that this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The comment text content written by the user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was originally created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted, null if active.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Audit trail for comment edits and version history.

This table captures point-in-time snapshots of comment content whenever edits are made. Each snapshot preserves the complete comment content and metadata as it existed at a specific moment, enabling version control and audit trail functionality. The table supports the 24-hour editing window requirement by maintaining historical versions that can be compared or restored.

Snapshots are automatically created when users edit their comments, capturing the full text content along with metadata about who made the edit and when. This provides administrators with a complete history of comment modifications for moderation purposes and allows users to see how comments have evolved over time.

Each snapshot references the original {@link discussion_board_comments.id} and the user who performed the edit through {@link discussion_board_users.id}. This denormalized snapshot includes all comment fields to capture the complete state at each version.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent comment. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who created this snapshot. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: version_number
plainFields.description: Sequential version number for this comment snapshot.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for creating this snapshot, such as 'edit' or 'moderation'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: comment_content
plainFields.description: The complete comment content as it existed at the time of the snapshot.

plainFields.name: comment_created_at
plainFields.description: Original comment creation timestamp captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: comment_updated_at
plainFields.description: Comment updated timestamp captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: comment_deleted_at
plainFields.description: Comment deletion timestamp if applicable at snapshot time.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_moderations
models.description:
Tracks administrator moderation actions performed on comments for audit and compliance purposes.

This table records all moderation activities that administrators perform on comments, including editing comment content, deleting comments, and other moderation actions. Each record represents a single moderation event with details about the action taken, the administrator who performed it, and the reason for the moderation.

The table serves as an audit trail for compliance requirements and provides transparency into moderation activities. Administrators can review moderation history to ensure consistent application of community guidelines.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment being moderated. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who performed the moderation action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed (edit, delete, approve, reject, etc.).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the moderation action, explaining why the action was taken.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the moderation action (pending, completed, reversed, etc.).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_reports
models.description:
Tracks user reports of inappropriate comments for community moderation.

When users encounter comments that violate community guidelines, they can submit reports that are reviewed by administrators. Each report captures the reporter's identity, the specific comment being reported, the reason for reporting, and the current moderation status.

Reports follow a workflow from pending review to resolution, with timestamps tracking when reports were submitted and when they were acted upon by moderators. This system enables community-driven content moderation while maintaining accountability through proper audit trails.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_users} (reporter), {@link discussion_board_comments} (reported content)

foreignFields.name: reporter_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who submitted the report. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: reported_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Comment that was reported for moderation. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: User-provided reason explaining why the comment was reported.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the report in the moderation workflow (pending, under_review, resolved).

plainFields.name: resolution_details
plainFields.description: Administrator's notes about how the report was resolved.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was resolved by an administrator.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_votes
models.description:
Tracks user votes on comments for quality assessment and community feedback.

Each vote represents a user's assessment of comment quality, supporting features like upvoting/downvoting and comment ranking. The system ensures users can only vote once per comment through unique constraints.

This table supports community-driven content quality assessment by allowing users to express approval or disapproval of comments. Votes contribute to comment ranking algorithms and help surface high-quality content. {@link discussion_board_comments.id} represents the comment being voted on, while {@link discussion_board_users.id} identifies the voting user.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who cast the vote. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Comment being voted on. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: Type of vote cast by the user. Valid values are 'upvote' for positive assessment and 'downvote' for negative assessment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was cast.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_attachments
models.description:
Junction table linking comments to their file attachments. This table establishes a many-to-many relationship between comments and files, allowing multiple files to be attached to multiple comments while maintaining referential integrity.

Each record represents a specific file attachment associated with a particular comment. The relationship ensures that files can be properly tracked and managed within the comment system, supporting features like file downloads and attachment management.

This table works in conjunction with {@link discussion_board_comments} for comment references and {@link discussion_board_article_files} for file references, providing the necessary linkage for comment attachment functionality.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment that this file is attached to. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_file_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the file attachment. {@link discussion_board_article_files.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attachment was linked to the comment.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_mentions
models.description:
Tracks user mentions within comment content for notification and reference purposes.

When users mention other users in comments using @mentions, this table records those references. Each mention includes the comment where it appears, the mentioned user, and the position within the comment text where the mention occurs. This enables features like notification systems that alert mentioned users and provides reference data for user activity tracking.

The table maintains a many-to-many relationship between comments and users, allowing multiple mentions per comment and multiple comments mentioning the same user. Position tracking supports features like highlighting mentions within comment text or determining context around the mention.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Comment containing the user mention. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who is mentioned in the comment. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: position_start
plainFields.description: Starting character position of the mention within the comment text.

plainFields.name: position_end
plainFields.description: Ending character position of the mention within the comment text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the mention was created.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_flags
models.description:
User-reported content flags for inappropriate or problematic comments requiring moderator review.

This table tracks user-submitted flags on comments that violate community guidelines or require administrator attention. Each flag represents a user's concern about specific comment content and includes the reason for flagging. Flags can be in various states (pending, reviewed, resolved) and help administrators identify problematic content efficiently.

Flags are created by users who identify inappropriate content and are reviewed by administrators for appropriate action. The system maintains a complete audit trail of flag creation, review, and resolution to ensure transparency and accountability in content moderation.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_users} (flag creator), {@link discussion_board_comments} (flagged content), {@link discussion_board_admins} (reviewer).

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who created the flag. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Comment being flagged for review. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who reviewed the flag. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: flag_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of why the comment was flagged by the user.

plainFields.name: flag_type
plainFields.description: Category of flag violation (spam, harassment, inappropriate, etc.).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the flag (pending, under_review, resolved, dismissed).

plainFields.name: resolution_notes
plainFields.description: Administrator's notes on how the flag was resolved.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the flag was created by the user.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the flag was reviewed by an administrator.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the flag was resolved.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_histories
models.description:
Tracks the complete edit history of comments with timestamps and content versions.

This table maintains an audit trail of all changes made to comments, capturing both the original content and edited versions. Each edit record includes the timestamp, editor information, and the specific changes made. This supports compliance requirements and provides transparency for comment modification tracking.

The edit history is managed through the parent {@link discussion_board_comments} entity and serves as a comprehensive record of content evolution. Administrators can review edit history for moderation purposes, and users can see the progression of their own comment edits.

Key relationships:
- References {@link discussion_board_comments} as the parent comment
- Editor attribution through specialized subtype tables

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent comment being edited. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

plainFields.name: edit_sequence
plainFields.description: Sequential number indicating the order of edits for this comment. First edit is 1, second is 2, etc.

plainFields.name: original_content
plainFields.description: The content of the comment before this edit was applied.

plainFields.name: edited_content
plainFields.description: The content of the comment after this edit was applied.

plainFields.name: edit_reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason provided by the editor for making this change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit was recorded.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_pagination_settings
models.description:
Stores pagination settings and comment count tracking for efficient loading of comments on articles.

This table maintains pagination configurations and comment counts for each article to optimize comment loading performance. It tracks the total comment count, pagination settings, and last update timestamp to ensure efficient comment retrieval without recalculating counts on every request.

The table supports the requirement for paginated comment display on articles, particularly when articles have more than 50 comments. By maintaining pre-calculated counts and pagination metadata, the system can quickly determine page boundaries and comment ranges for display.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Associated article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: comments_per_page
plainFields.description: Number of comments to display per page for pagination.

plainFields.name: total_comment_count
plainFields.description: Current total number of comments on the article.

plainFields.name: last_comment_count_update
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment count was last updated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the pagination settings were created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the pagination settings were last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_rate_limits
models.description:
Tracks comment submission rates for spam prevention and rate limiting.

This table stores submission timestamps for each user to enforce rate limiting rules. The system uses this data to prevent spam and abusive behavior by limiting users to 10 comments per minute as specified in the requirements.

Each record represents a single comment submission attempt. The system queries this table to determine if a user has exceeded the rate limit within the specified time window.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user who submitted the comment. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment submission was attempted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limit record was created.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_of_users
models.description:
Maps comment edit history records to regular user editors, maintaining referential integrity for user-attributed edits.

This table establishes the relationship between comment edit history records and the regular users who performed the edits. It ensures proper ownership tracking and maintains referential integrity for user-attributed comment modifications. Each record represents a specific edit action performed by a regular user on a comment.

The table supports the polymorphic ownership pattern for comment edit history, allowing different actor types (users, admins, super admins) to have their own subtype tables while maintaining a unified edit history system. This design ensures that edit attribution is properly tracked and cannot be accidentally assigned to multiple actor types.

{@link discussion_board_comment_edit_histories.id} provides the edit history context, while {@link discussion_board_users.id} identifies the regular user who performed the edit. The unique constraint ensures that each edit history record can only be attributed to one user editor.

This table is essential for tracking user contributions to comment content and supporting the 24-hour editing window requirement specified in the system requirements.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment edit history record being attributed to a user editor. {@link discussion_board_comment_edit_histories.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the regular user who performed the comment edit. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the edit attribution record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the edit attribution record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_of_admins
models.description:
Maps comment edit history records to admin editors, maintaining referential integrity for admin-attributed edits.

This table establishes the relationship between comment edit history records and the administrators who performed those edits. It ensures proper polymorphic ownership pattern where edit history can be attributed to different types of editors (users, admins, super admins) while maintaining database integrity.

The table serves as a junction between the comment edit history system and the administrator authorization system, allowing administrators to have their edit actions properly recorded and tracked. This supports audit trails and accountability for content modifications performed by administrators.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment edit history record being attributed to an admin editor. {@link discussion_board_comment_edit_histories.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who performed the edit. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit attribution record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit attribution record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_of_super_admins
models.description:
Maps comment edit history records to super admin editors, maintaining referential integrity for super admin-attributed edits.

This subtype table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comment editing by super administrators. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship between a comment edit history entry and the super administrator who performed the edit, ensuring proper attribution and audit trail integrity.

When a super administrator edits a comment, this table links the resulting edit history record to the specific super admin, allowing the system to track which administrator made each modification. This supports accountability and compliance requirements for content moderation workflows.

This table works alongside similar subtype tables for regular users and regular administrators, providing a complete polymorphic ownership solution for comment editing attribution across all actor types.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_edit_history_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment edit history record being attributed to a super admin editor. {@link discussion_board_comment_edit_histories.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the super administrator who performed the comment edit. {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attribution mapping was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this attribution mapping was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_promotion_requests
models.description:
Tracks administrator promotion requests with workflow status and approval tracking.

This table stores the complete lifecycle of administrator promotion requests, from initial submission through super administrator review to final decision. Each request includes the user's justification for seeking administrator status, current workflow state, and timestamps for audit purposes. The table supports the hierarchical administrator system by enabling super administrators to review and process promotion requests according to platform governance policies.

Promotion requests transition through pending, approved, or rejected states, with detailed tracking of decision timestamps and reviewer information. This ensures compliance with the administrator promotion process requirements and maintains a complete audit trail of all promotion activities.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who submitted the promotion request. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator record created when request is approved, or null if pending/rejected. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: User-provided justification for seeking administrator status, between 50-500 characters as required.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current workflow status: 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was approved by a super administrator.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was rejected by a super administrator.

plainFields.name: reviewer_discussion_board_super_admin_id
plainFields.description: Super administrator who reviewed and decided on the promotion request. {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id}

plainFields.name: reviewer_notes
plainFields.description: Optional notes from the super administrator explaining the approval or rejection decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was initially submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_administrators
models.description:
Central record for administrator assignments and grade management. Tracks which users have administrator privileges, their current grade level (regular or super administrator), and maintains promotion/demotion history. This table serves as the authoritative source for administrator status across the platform.

Each record represents an administrator assignment for a specific user, linking to the appropriate authentication tables based on the current grade level. The table supports the hierarchical administrator system where super administrators can promote regular administrators and manage grade changes.

{@link discussion_board_users.id} provides the base user identity, while {@link discussion_board_admins.id} and {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id} link to the appropriate authentication tables based on the current administrator grade.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user's base identity. {@link discussion_board_users.id}

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to regular administrator authentication when applicable. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

foreignFields.name: super_admin_id
